mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds Rate rises by at least 0.25 percentage points over the next month, the S&P 500 forward 20-day return is expected to turn negative due to tightened financing conditions for corporate investment.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increases by ≥ 0.25 pp over the next 30 calendar days
failure_condition: In sample periods where FEDFUNDS rises by ≥ 0.25 pp but SPX 20d returns are not statistically lower than the prior month (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in unemployment benefits applications (PAYEMS) accompanied by a simultaneous decline in consumer demand (HOUST) predicts negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as weak labor market support coexists with falling business activity.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases for ≥ 3 consecutive months while HOUST decreases by ≥ 5% over the same horizon
regime_hint: Labor slack and demand weakness coexist
failure_condition: Over 60-day horizon, SPX 20d returns are not significantly negative relative to the pre-signal period (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in industrial production (INDPRO) exceeding 5% over the next 2 months signals accelerating supply capacity, which typically precedes a positive S&P 500 forward return within 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO increases by > 5% over the next 60 calendar days
failure_condition: SPX 20d returns are not statistically positive (p > 0.05) during the 2-month INDPRO expansion window.

mechanism_narrative: When consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) remains above 2.5% for three consecutive months, the S&P 500 forward 5-day return is expected to be negative due to expectations of prolonged tight monetary policy.
failure_condition: Over the 5-day horizon, SPX returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.05) despite CPIAUCSL staying above 2.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 4.0% for 10 consecutive months, without a corresponding rise in consumer price inflation, predicts a positive S&P 500 forward return over the next 20 days as labor market tightening supports equity valuations.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 4.0% for ≥ 10 consecutive months and CPIAUCSL < 2.5% over the same period
regime_hint: Labor market tightening with stable inflation
failure_condition: SPX 20d returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.05) during the 10-month UNRATE contraction.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden drop in retail employment (PAYEMS) by at least 10% in a single month coincides with a sharp rise in manufacturing payrolls (RSAFS), predicting a negative S&P 500 forward return over the next 60 days due to sector reallocation away from retail.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS falls by ≥ 10% in a single month while RSAFS increases by ≥ 15% in the following month
regime_hint: Sector reallocation from retail to manufacturing
failure_condition: SPX 20d returns over the 60-day window are not significantly negative (p > 0.05) despite the observed employment shifts.

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive 2-month decline in consumer demand measured by HOUST below 1,200 units predicts a positive S&P 500 forward return over the next 20 days as persistent weakness in household spending signals a bottom in economic activity.
failure_condition: SPX 20d returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.05) during the 2-month HOUST decline.

mechanism_narrative: When the monthly change in the GDP deflator (not directly observable here, but as a proxy we use the inverse relationship between FEDFUNDS and inflation expectations) turns negative after a persistent positive trend for 3 months, the S&P 500 forward 60-day return is expected to be positive as investors anticipate easing inflation pressures.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS shows a downward trend for ≥ 3 consecutive months
regime_hint: Transition from inflationary to disinflationary monetary policy
failure_condition: SPX 20d returns over the 60-day window are not significantly positive (p > 0.05) despite the FEDFUNDS downtrend.
